advisory: Structural-only pre-1955 projection, not a complete 1920 Missal corpus. Only six Holy Week departures and the exact absences of St Joseph the Worker and the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary are established here. Every unstated formulary is served mechanically from roman-1962 without target-recension collation and must be described as inherited and uncollated rather than complete for 1920.

slices.basis: Accounting boundary for the pre-1955 recension. Its witness, accepted by maintainer decision on 2026-10-19, is the registered Bonn 2004 reimpressio of a conformed edition of about 1954 (artifact pp. 1-1220), with the 1922 Mame conformed printing as control. Every artifact page is assigned to a section slice or an explicit extent boundary (seam table in the source review), and identities absent from the 1922 control sit in separate post-1922-additions slices. Mass formularies and Preface identities are enumerated across the whole book, confirmed by an independent page-image review on 2026-10-19. The whole-book Mass-formulary denominator is the form rows of the temporal, sanctoral, body Commons/Marian/votive/dead, local-proper and local-Commons slices, post-1922 slices included (604); the devotional preparation/thanksgiving entries (23) share the kind but are not formularies, and oration-only and rite headings are prayer-set and exceptional-rite rows. The Preface denominator is the 13 rows of roman-pre-1955-prefaces plus the 2 Preface rows of roman-pre-1955-ordinary-post-1922-additions (15); the 1861 Cummiskey slice is other-witness evidence and is never summed with them. Text slots, Ordinary options, celebrations, commemorations, Commons as a kind and exceptional rites are not enumerated across the whole book. The positive slices remain subsets at their declared granularity; their union is not a text-slot denominator and this slice has no invented target count.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Eleven Preface identities printed in the 1861 Cummiskey lay witness section, not an enumeration of the 1920 target altar book. Target correspondence remains unresolved. slices.basis: Every dated Kalendarium entry of the Bonn witness, artifact pp. 26-36 (printed 26*-36*), whose identity the Mame 1922 control witness also carries: one celebration per principal clause (vigils included), one commemoration per printed Com. clause, split at ac/et between distinct identities and never within one companion group, and the rankless 12-05 Commemoratio S. Sabbæ. Octave, vigil and feria commemorations are kept as identities, labelled with their bracketed owner. Eleven dated Bonn identities with no 1922 counterpart are in the post-1922 additions slice. Movable entries printed inside the months are a separate slice. Labels normalize glyph losses (Purificatio, Transfiguratio, filiorum) and two misprints (Damiani, Alexandri). Mame's Kalendarium leaf for May 7-Jul 10 is missing from its scan; that range was compared against the Mame Proprium Sanctorum instead. Calendar identities only, not formularies, slots or text coverage; no calendar_mass_key joins are asserted.
slices.date_range: Pre-1955 recension as printed in the Bonn reimpressio (conformed c. 1954); post-1922 additions are in separate -post-1922-additions slices; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Independent reading of Ordo Missae (artifact pp. 375-381, printed 271-277) and Canon Missae through the Last Gospel (pp. 439-453, printed 335-349), with the Preface dialogue and Sanctus taken from the first Preface without chant (pp. 426-427). Named prayer blocks and dialogue turns at the granularity of the roman-1962-ordinary-text-blocks slice; repeated identical words in one block are one identity; proper-text appointments are form-referral rows. Mame 1922 (artifact pp. 385-470) prints the same blocks. An OCR phrase search located most of them; the six that OCR damage hid were confirmed on images at artifact pp. 386-387, 455, 458 and 465. Mame prints the seasonal Communicantes with the Prefaces, not inside the Canon (artifact p. 455). Differences from 1962: Benedicamus Domino is the alternative dismissal by quality of Mass (no procession form), and there is no episcopal Pax vobis in the Ordo. Page 438 is the Canon plate. Movement rubrics and notation are outside this denominator.
slices.date_range: Pre-1955 recension as printed in the Bonn reimpressio (conformed c. 1954); post-1922 additions are in separate -post-1922-additions slices; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All explicit wording alternatives in the Preface section (rubrics and texts, artifact pp. 426-437, repeated in the chant sections) and the Canon's seasonal Communicantes and Hanc igitur (pp. 440-441): two Nativity and two Easter Communicantes wordings, Epiphany, Ascension and Pentecost, the shared continuation, one Hanc igitur insertion, three Easter Preface wordings, the Holy Spirit insertion and its omission, ten Marian and two Josephine occasion words. The Joseph Preface has two occasions, not 1962's three: the May 1 feast does not exist. Mame 1922 prints the same 26 alternatives. It places each seasonal Communicantes and the Hanc igitur insertion after its Preface without chant, not in the Canon. Image-checked at Mame artifact pp. 447 (Easter Hanc igitur, Ascension Communicantes) and 450 (Marian occasions); the rest were located by OCR.

slices.basis: The thirteen Bonn Preface identities also printed in Mame 1922: Nativity, Epiphany, Lent, Holy Cross, Easter, Ascension, Holy Spirit, Trinity, BVM, St Joseph, Apostles, Common and the Dead. They are enumerated across all three Bonn presentations: solemn tone pp. 382-403 (14 Prefaces), ferial tone pp. 404-425 (15) and without chant pp. 426-437 (15); together these name exactly 15 identities. Sacred Heart and Christ the King are in the post-1922 additions slice. Chant presentations and the rubrics prefixed to each Preface do not multiply identities. Reconciliation: the eleven roman-pre-1955-cummiskey-prefaces rows are another witness (1861) of eleven of these identities. They are not added again, and Holy Cross remains distinct from the Passiontide use of the same Preface.

slices.basis: Printed musical presentations in Ordo Missae and Canon (artifact pp. 377-451): four Gloria intonations, one Credo intonation, two Pater noster tones, one Pax tone and eleven dismissal tones (I-XI). Also the solemn and ferial Preface presentations of the Prefaces present in 1922: 12 solemn and 12 ferial (the Dead has only a ferial tone). The without-chant section is the spoken presentation and owns the Preface identities and wording options, as in the 1962 model; it adds no musical option. The Bonn witness has eleven dismissal tones where Mame 1922 has twelve: Mame's separate tones for ferias per annum and for Advent/Lent ferias are one Bonn tone VIII.

slices.basis: A complete reading of Ritus servandus (artifact pp. 60-76, printed 60*-76*), deduplicated against the Ordo lane, gives sixteen positive textual appointments: 5 wording alternatives and 11 contextual slots. Before the 1960 change the communion of the faithful carried its own Confiteor, Misereatur and Indulgentiam (in the vestrorum form). These three rows have no 1962 counterpart. A separate placement of the same words counts as a separate appointment, following the 1962 precedent for Domine, non sum dignus. Excluded: movement rubrics, omission rules, repeated Ordo formulas (Suscipiat fallback, Pax tecum, Dona eis requiem) and the prelate's blessing, which is a variant gesture. Mame 1922 prints the same appointments; an OCR search was spot-checked against its Ritus at artifact pp. 73-87.
slices.date_range: Pre-1955 recension as printed in the Bonn reimpressio (conformed c. 1954); post-1922 additions are in separate -post-1922-additions slices; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All 23 printed entry headings of Praeparatio ad Missam and Gratiarum actio post Missam, artifact pp. 83-101 (printed 83*-101*), including the seven-day Ambrose set and all three vesting modes. These are devotional forms, not Mass formularies. Mame 1922 (artifact pp. 94-112) prints the same 23 entries, in the same order apart from Oblatio sui preceding En ego. Neither witness prints the Oratio universalis attributed to Clement XI, which the 1962 book adds. The printed indulgence notes are dated 1858-1917 and are not entries.
slices.date_range: Pre-1955 recension as printed in the Bonn reimpressio (conformed c. 1954); post-1922 additions are in separate -post-1922-additions slices; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All 91 semantic appointments within the 23 entries, at the granularity of the roman-1962-preparation-thanksgiving-slots slice. Psalms, canticle and antiphons, Kyrie sets, the Pater noster with its final response, versicle-response pairs, orations, seven weekday prayers, and 7 priest, 15 pontifical-bishop and 9 private-bishop vesting prayers. Repeated antiphons count once per form. Embedded doxologies, Amen, Oremus and the seasonal Alleluia stay with their parent appointment. Semantic source slots only; no wording collation or English coverage is claimed.
slices.date_range: Pre-1955 recension as printed in the Bonn reimpressio (conformed c. 1954); post-1922 additions are in separate -post-1922-additions slices; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Source-derived enumeration of the accepted pre-1955 witness (Bonn 2004 reimpressio of the 28th edition iuxta typicam Vaticanam, SHA-256 b676ce5c…a1d, a conformed printing of about 1954) from p. 105, which opens the Proprium de Tempore after the plate on p. 104, through the Saturday after Passion Sunday on p. 273 (p. 274 is a plate). The book prints no marginal unit numbers; every printed formulary heading is a form (Advent Ember Saturday has a single form; the three octave-day headings of 2–4 January and the Telesphorus heading are referral-only forms; the Hyginus heading carries proper orations with a Common referral). Every printed proper role is one text-slot: Introit with psalm, each oration, each lesson, Gradual, Alleluia with verse, Tract, Hymnus, Gospel, Offertory, Secret, Communion, Postcommunion and Oratio super populum; votive and paschal alternatives printed inside a formulary are distinct slots. Printed commemorations are slots of their form; the Orationes pro diversitate Temporum blocks are prayer-sets of three slots. Preface, Communicantes and Hanc igitur appointments, Credo, Gloria, Flectamus genua and dismissal directions are positive text-slots; printed referrals (seasonal orations ut supra, Common or feast Masses, ferial reuse) are form-referrals. The ashes rite is an exceptional-rite with its slots. Roles were read from the typeset text layer by style (red role headings, reading titles, drop capitals) and checked on page images at every doubtful heading. Every formulary has a counterpart in the 1922 Mame control witness (Holy Family and Hyginus are printed in its Proprium de Sanctis). No held propers or 1962 rows were used.
slices.date_range: Bonn reimpressio artifact pp. 105–273 (printed 1–169): Dominica I Adventus through Sabbato post Dominicam Passionis

slices.basis: The pre-1955 (pre-Maxima redemptionis) Holy Week of the accepted Bonn witness, enumerated in named semantic blocks at the granularity of the 1962 Holy Week lane: seven day celebrations; Mass forms for Palm Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Maundy Thursday and Holy Saturday; four exceptional rites (blessing, distribution and procession of palms; the Thursday reposition, stripping of altars and Mandatum; the Good Friday lessons, nine solemn orations, adoration of the Cross and Mass of the Presanctified; the Holy Saturday blessings of fire and incense, Lumen Christi, Exsultet, twelve prophecies, blessing of the font and litany) with their units and printed slots. Named but unprinted texts (Pange lingua on Thursday, Psalm 21, Asperges, Rituale baptism) are form-referrals. No Chrism Mass is printed. Supersedes the 1862 Pustet / 1951–1954 composite tracer slices for target correspondence; see the lane review for the unit mapping.
slices.date_range: Bonn reimpressio artifact pp. 275–373 (printed 171–269): Dominica in Palmis through Sabbato Sancto

slices.basis: Same method and granularity as the Advent-to-Passiontide slice, from Easter Sunday on p. 455 (after the plate on p. 454) through the last Sunday after Pentecost on p. 581 (p. 582 is a plate; p. 583 opens the Proprium de Sanctis). Includes the Pentecost vigil with its six prophecies, tracts, orations, font procession and Mass, the September Ember days, the four resumed Sundays after Epiphany and the Corpus Christi and Sacred Heart octave Sundays. The Sacred Heart feast formulary and its octave appointments are held in the post-1922 slice.
slices.date_range: Bonn reimpressio artifact pp. 455–581 (printed 351–477): Dominica Resurrectionis through Dominica XXIV et ultima post Pentecosten

slices.basis: Temporal identities printed in the Bonn witness with no counterpart in the 1922 Mame control (artifact record src/sources/works/catholic-church/missale-romanum/editions/1922-tours-mame-editio-quarta-iuxta-typicam/artifacts/ia-scan-pdf-9873693a/artifact.toml): the formulary In Festo Sacratissimi Cordis Jesu (Introit Cogitationes, with octave of the third order) printed on Friday after the Octave of Corpus Christi, its octave referrals, and the Sacred Heart octave commemorations and Preface appointment printed in the Sunday within that octave. Mame 1922 prints a different Sacred Heart formulary (Introit Miserebitur) in its Proprium de Sanctis (artifact p. 720, printed p. 606) and the third Sunday after Pentecost without an octave (artifact pp. 540–541). Institution or decree date: not established (printed in neither witness; no registered source states it). Post-1930 rights split: these rows identify text the 2026-10-19 public-domain decision may not reach.
slices.date_range: Bonn reimpressio artifact pp. 527–531; absent from the 1922 Mame temporal and sanctoral

slices.basis: Every dated or movable formulary heading and separately headed nested votive formulary in the Proprium de Sanctis, artifact pp. 583-965 / printed pp. 479-861 (p. 966 is an unnumbered plate) that also has a counterpart in the Proprium de Sanctis of the 1922 Mame editio quarta iuxta typicam: 327 identities. The three All Souls Masses are separate forms; the 2 February Mass under 'Ad Missam' belongs to the Purification form; five rubric-only date headings (28 Nov., 1 Dec., 14 Dec., 19 Dec., 27 Jun.) are not forms. Referral-only dated headings ('Missa ... de Communi', 'Pro S. N.') are forms. Seasonal sub-variants inside a formulary, including the second printed Masses of 1 and 12 May, stay inside one form. Three identities print on another day than in Mame 1922 (Peter Nolasco 28 Jan., Hedwig 16 Oct., Gertrude 16 Nov.); their loci say so. Thirteen identities absent from Mame 1922's Proprium are in roman-pre-1955-sanctoral-post-1922-additions. Derived from the clean text layer in reading order and checked on page images at every seam and doubtful heading.
slices.date_range: Pre-1955 recension (nominal 1920 typical edition) as witnessed by the Bonn 2004 reimpressio of the 28th edition iuxta typicam, a conformed printing of about 1954; historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Every printed role heading under the 327 forms of roman-pre-1955-sanctoral-body-forms in the Proprium de Sanctis, artifact pp. 583-965 / printed pp. 479-861 (p. 966 is an unnumbered plate): Introit, Collect, Epistle or lesson, Gradual, Alleluia, Tract, Sequence, Gospel, Offertory, Secret, Communion and Postcommunion, each printed heading once, including seasonal and votive alternative chants, alternative Collects, commemoration orations (named by a 'Pro N.' heading or an introducing commemoration rubric, or by position after the main oration) and printed third orations. These are contextual appointments, not distinct wording identities. Role headings referred elsewhere are form-referral rows; Prefaces are a separate slice; orations merely named in rubrics are not slots. Text-layer typographic variants of headings (Postcummunio, Offertórium, Seqientia) were included by pattern and the role sequence of every form was checked for completeness.

slices.basis: Positive referral loci at line start within the forms of roman-pre-1955-sanctoral-body-forms in the Proprium de Sanctis, artifact pp. 583-965 / printed pp. 479-861 (p. 966 is an unnumbered plate): formulary referrals ('Missa N., de Communi ...', 'Missa ut in Festo', 'Omnia dicuntur sicut ...', seasonal 'Tempore Paschali Missa ...'), infra-octave referrals, votive-use rubrics that send a role or the Mass elsewhere, and role-level referrals ('Epistola ... ut supra'). translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n1316, ordinary printed p. 1302, under the Common of One or More Supreme Pontiffs and `Prayer`. The facing Latin is the 1962 singular Collect with its martyr alternative intact. This is ordinary numbered matter immediately before, and not part of, excluded pp. 1302a-1302d; no other Supreme-Pontiff row is recovered.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O eternal Shepherd, do Thou look favorably upon Thy flock, which we beseech Thee to guard and keep for evermore through the Blessed N. (Thy Martyr and) Supreme Pontiff, whom Thou didst choose to be the chief shepherd of the whole Church. Through Our Lord.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins on leaf n1365, printed p. 1347, and finishes on leaf n1366, printed p. 1348. The witness prints one Secret with `Pontificis (vel Confessoris)` and `bishop (or confessor)` in the facing columns. This exact row keeps that printed alternative while addressing the 1962 Pontiff branch; it does not silently resolve or compose the parenthesis.

translations.caution:

Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.text: O God, Who dost invisibly contain all things, and yet dost visibly show the signs of Thy power for the salvation of mankind, illumine this temple by the virtue of Thine indwelling, and grant that all who assemble here to pray, from whatsoever tribulation they shall call upon Thee, may obtain the blessings of Thy consolation. Through our Lord.

Through our Lord.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

Read at printed pp. 138-142 = leaves n175-n179. The book's Missal section does not reprint this sequence: printed p. 244 directs `For Stabat Mater dolorosa, see page 138.`, and p. 138 heads it `Friday after Passion-Sunday. FEAST OF THE SEVEN DOLOURS OF THE BLESSED VIRGIN MARY. VESPERS.` with the incipit `Stabat Mater dolorosa.`, continued under `MATINS (The same continued.)` at p. 140 and `LAUDS (The same continued.)` at p. 141. The three hours together carry the twenty strophes of the Missal sequence with no doxology added at any break, and the last stanza renders both `Christe, cum sit hinc exire` and `Quando corpus morietur`, which is the Missal's ending and not the Breviary hymn's. Ten stanzas against twenty strophes, two for one. The Missal's closing `Amen.` is not rendered.

translations.text:
At the Cross her station keeping,
Stood the mournful Mother weeping,
Close to Jesus to the last:
Through her heart, his sorrow sharing,
All his bitter anguish bearing,
Now at length the sword had pass’d.

Oh, how sad and sore distress’d
Was that Mother highly blest
Of the sole-begotten One!
Christ above in torment hangs;
She beneath beholds the pangs
Of her dying glorious Son.

Is there one who would not weep,
Whelm’d in miseries so deep
Christ’s dear Mother to behold?
Can the human heart refrain
From partaking in her pain,
In that Mother’s pain untold?

Bruis’d, derided, curs’d, defil’d,
She beheld her tender Child
All with bloody scourges rent;
For the sins of his own nation,
Saw Him hang in desolation,
Till his Spirit forth He sent.

O thou Mother! fount of love!
Touch my spirit from above,
Make my heart with thine accord:
Make me feel as thou hast felt;
Make my soul to glow and melt
With the love of Christ my Lord.

Holy Mother! pierce me through;
In my heart each wound renew
Of my Saviour crucified:
Let me share with thee His pain,
Who for all my sins was slain,
Who for me in torments died.

Let me mingle tears with thee,
Mourning Him who mourn’d for me,
All the days that I may live:
By the Cross with thee to stay;
There with thee to weep and pray;
Is all I ask of thee to give.

Virgin of all virgins best!
Listen to my fond request:
Let me share thy grief divine;
Let me, to my latest breath,
In my body bear the death
Of that dying Son of thine.

Wounded with his every wound,
Steep my soul till it hath swoon’d
In his very blood away;
Be to me, O Virgin, nigh,
Lest in flames I burn and die,
In his awful Judgment day.

Christ, when Thou shalt call me hence,
Be thy Mother my defence,
Be thy Cross my victory;
While my body here decays,
May my soul thy goodness praise,
Safe in Paradise with Thee.

A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n672, printed p. 664, running head `23d, 24th AND 26th SEPTEMBER`, heading `XXIV. B. V. MARY of Mercy.`, rubric `All as in the Votive Mass, Salve, p. 507, except`. translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n565, printed p. 557, running head `8th AND 10th FEBRUARY`, heading `VIII. St. JOHN of MATHA, c.`, rubric `All as in Mass XIII. p. 488, except`. Latin cue `Deus.`, answering `Deus, qui per sanctum Joannem`. A bounded page-image collation confirms the complete target identity. For All Souls this is the first 2-November form only; the second and third forms remain quarantined for substantive wording differences.

Thro'.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n912, printed p. 914, running head `FEB. 9-ST. CYRIL OF ALEXANDRIA, B. C.`, under `Prayer` in the Mass headed `St. Cyril of Alexandria, Bishop, Confessor, Doctor of the Church`. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer; the witness spells `Genitricem` where 1962 spells `Genetricem` and prints the conclusion cue `Per eumdem Dominum` where 1962 expands the conclusion. The book itself prints Cyril's name, title and English, so no name or wording is supplied by this inventory.

translations.text: O God, Who didst make blessed Cyril, Thy Confessor and Bishop, the invincible champion of the most blessed Virgin Mary's divine maternity, grant through his intercession that we, who verily believe her to be the Mother of God, may be saved by her maternal protection. Through the same.

The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1861 prints one Mass for both Chairs of St Peter. Leaf n546, printed p. 538, heads it `XVIII. St. PETER's CHAIR at ROME, &c.` and rubricates `By omitting the COMM. of St. Prisca +, this Mass serves also for his Chair at Antioch on the 22d February.`, so the 22 February commemoration of St Paul is the `Of St. PAUL` oration printed here. Latin cue `Deus, qui multitudinem.` The Kalendar at leaf n775, printed p. 767, sends 22 February to the same p. 538. A bounded page-image collation confirms the complete target identity. For All Souls this is the first 2-November form only; the second and third forms remain quarantined for substantive wording differences.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: O God, who by the preaching of blessed Paul the Apostle, didst instruct the multitude of the Gentiles: grant, we beseech thee, that whilst we celebrate his memory, we may find the effects of his prayers. Thro'.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 12 March Mass begins on leaf n570, printed p. 562, headed `XII. St. GREGORY, p. c.`, and its Secret and Postcommunion stand at the head of leaf n571, printed p. 563, under the running head `17th AND 19th MARCH`. The Secret is set with no Latin cue; it answers `Annue nobis, quaesumus`. A bounded page-image collation confirms the complete target identity. For All Souls this is the first 2-November form only; the second and third forms remain quarantined for substantive wording differences.

A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins on leaf n1365, printed p. 1347, and finishes on leaf n1366, printed p. 1348. The witness prints one Secret with `Pontificis (vel Confessoris)` and `bishop (or confessor)` in the facing columns. This exact row keeps that printed alternative while addressing the 1962 Pontiff branch; it does not silently resolve or compose the parenthesis.

Leaf n592, printed p. 584, heads 14 May `XIV. St. BONIFACE, m.` and rubricates `All as in Mass V. p. 470, except COLLECT. Da, quaesumus.` -- so the day prints its own Collect only, and its Secret is Mass V's. Mass V is `Protexisti`, of a Martyr in Paschal time; leaf n480, printed p. 472, prints under it `SECRET. Of a Martyr not a Bishop.` with no name in it, word for word the 1962's `Muneribus nostris, quaesumus Domine`. Boniface is a martyr and not a bishop, and 14 May falls in Paschal time, so that is the form the pointer reaches. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

Leaf n1044, printed p. 1052, running head `JUNE 18-ST. EPHREM`, under `Prayer` in the Mass headed `St. Ephrem the Syrian, Deacon, Confessor and Doctor of the Church`. The Latin agrees with the 1962 slot in every syllable and abbreviates only the conclusion to `Per Dominum`.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The same one Secret on leaves n1365-n1366 prints `Pontificis (vel Confessoris)` and `bishop (or confessor)`. This exact row keeps the printed alternative while addressing the 1962 non-Pontiff branch; one reading of one passage therefore supports both exact branch identities without inventing either wording.

propers.incipit: Deus, qui beato Petro Apostolo tuo
propers.name: Collect

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Two pointers reach this text. Leaf n617, printed p. 609, heads 30 June `XXX. COMMEMORATION of St. PAUL.` and rubricates `All as on January 25, p. 543`; leaf n552, printed p. 544, then prints for 25 January `Of St. PETER, Deus, qui beato, as on the Feast of his Chair at Rome, the 18th of January, p. 538.` The oration itself stands on leaf n546, printed p. 538, with the Latin cue `Deus, qui beato.` The 1962 index reprints the same three orations under 01-25 and 06-30, and this file already records them at comm-s-petri-apostoli; the English is therefore recorded twice, as at the three commemorations named in the 1962 open_collation_items. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.text: O God, who by delivering to the blessed apostle Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, didst give him the power of binding and loosing: grant that, by his intercession, we may be freed from the bonds of our sins. Who livest.

A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n627, printed p. 619, keeps 18 July as `XVIII. St. CAMILLUS de LELLIS, c.` and rubricates `Commem. of St. SYMPHOROSA, &c. by the Collect, &c. of Mass VIII. p. 477.` Mass VIII is `Sapientiam`, of Many Martyrs; its Secret, on leaf n487, printed p. 479, carries no name at all and answers the 1962's `Munera tibi, Domine, nostrae devotionis offerimus` word for word. Its Collect and Postcommunion do carry `N. and N.` and are ledgered untranslated. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins on leaf n1365, printed p. 1347, and finishes on leaf n1366, printed p. 1348. The witness prints one Secret with `Pontificis (vel Confessoris)` and `bishop (or confessor)` in the facing columns. This exact row keeps that printed alternative while addressing the 1962 Pontiff branch; it does not silently resolve or compose the parenthesis.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins on leaf n1158, printed p. 1166, under `Prayer` in the Mass headed `St. John Eudes, Confessor`, and finishes on leaf n1159, printed p. 1167; both leaves were opened. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer word for word, differing only in pointing and the witness's abbreviated conclusion `Per eumdem Dominum`.

Through the same.

propers.incipit: Munera tibi, Domine, nostrae devotionis offerimus
propers.name: Secret

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n672, printed p. 664, heads 26 September `XXVI. SS. CYPRIAN and JUSTINA, mm.`, rubricates `All as in Mass IX. p. 479, except` a proper Collect, and then names `SECRET, (We bring) and P. Comm.(Praesta.) p. 479` -- addressing the two orations by their opening words on that page. `We bring` is Mass VIII's Secret, on leaf n487, printed p. 479, which carries no name and answers the 1962's `Munera tibi, Domine, nostrae devotionis offerimus` word for word. `Praesta` on the same page carries `N. and N.` and is ledgered untranslated. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n679, printed p. 671, heads 5 October `V. SS. PLACIDUS and COMPANIONS, mm.` and rubricates `All as in Mass IX. p. 479, except the Collect, Secret. and P. Comm. which are taken from Mass VIII. pp. 478, 479.` Mass VIII's Secret, on leaf n487, printed p. 479, carries no name and answers `Munera tibi, Domine, nostrae devotionis offerimus` word for word. Its Collect and Postcommunion carry `N. and N.` and the Postcommunion is ledgered untranslated. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. Leaf n1316, ordinary printed p. 1302, under the Common of One or More Supreme Pontiffs and `Prayer`. The facing Latin is the 1962 singular Collect with its martyr alternative intact. translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

Read at printed pp. 241-244 = leaves n278-n281, under `Sequence, Mass for the Dead.` and the incipit `Dies irae dies illa.` Nineteen stanzas against the Missal's nineteen strophes, one for one; the closing `Amen.` is not rendered. This corrected the recovered lane brief and the then-current guidance row, which had misidentified the London edition's contents. The London 1849 prints it, in its Missal section, between the Lauda Sion and the cross-reference to the Stabat Mater. An independent English of this sequence is therefore not needed for coverage; the alternative Irons text below is offered as a choice of voice, not as a gap-filler. The existing untranslated row for this slot refuses the 1861 witness's own English as a verse paraphrase in the manner of Roscommon; that refusal stands and is not disturbed by this row, which comes from a different book.

translations.text:
Nigher still, and still more nigh
Draws the Day of Prophecy,
Doom’d to melt the earth and sky.

Oh, what trembling there shall be,
When the world its Judge shall see,
Coming in dread majesty!

Hark! the trump, with thrilling tone,
From sepulchral regions lone,
Summons all before the throne:

Time and Death it doth appal,
To see the buried ages all
Rise to answer at the call.

Now the books are open spread;
Now the writing must be read,
Which condemns the quick and dead:

Now, before the Judge severe
Hidden things must all appear;
Nought can pass unpunish’d here.

What shall guilty I then plead?
Who for me will intercede,
When the Saints shall comfort need?

King of dreadful Majesty!
Who dost freely justify!
Fount of Pity, save Thou me!

Recollect, O Love divine!
’Twas for this lost sheep of thine
Thou thy glory didst resign:

Satest wearied seeking me;
Sufferedst upon the Tree:
Let not vain thy labour be.

Judge of Justice, hear my prayer!
Spare me, Lord, in mercy spare!
Ere the Reckoning-day appear.

Lo! thy gracious face I seek;
Shame and grief are on my cheek;
Sighs and tears my sorrow speak.

Thou didst Mary’s guilt forgive;
Didst the dying thief receive;
Hence doth hope within me live.

Worthless are my prayers, I know;
Yet, oh, cause me not to go
Into everlasting woe.

Sever’d from the guilty band,
Make me with thy sheep to stand,
Placing me on thy right hand.

When the curs’d in anguish flee
Into flames of misery;
With the Blest then call Thou me.

Suppliant in the dust I lie;
My heart a cinder, crush’d and dry;
Help me, Lord, when death is nigh!

Full of tears, and full of dread,
Is the day that wakes the dead,
Calling all, with solemn blast,
From the ashes of the past.

Lord of mercy! Jesu blest!
Grant the Faithful light and rest.

OWN. That book's compilers are widely said to have altered what they received;
this lane established no instance of alteration in this hymn and ran no collation

of the transcription.

translations.text:
Day of Wrath! O day of mourning!
See fulfill’d the prophets’ warning!
Heav’n and earth in ashes burning!
Oh, what fear man’s bosom rendeth
When from Heav’n the Judge descendeth,
On Whose sentence all dependeth!

Wondrous sound the trumpet flingeth,
Through earth’s sepulchres it ringeth,
All before the Throne it bringeth.
Death is struck, and nature quaking,
All creation is awaking,
To its Judge an answer making.

Lo! the Book exactly worded,
Wherein all hath been recorded;
Thence shall judgment be awarded.
When the Judge His seat attaineth,
And each hidden deed arraigneth,
Nothing unavenged remaineth.

What shall I, frail man, be pleading,
Who for me be interceding,
When the just are mercy needing?
King of Majesty tremendous,
Who dost free salvation send us,
Fount of pity, then befriend us!

Think, good Jesu, my salvation
Caused Thy wondrous Incarnation;
Leave me not to reprobation.
Faint and weary Thou hast sought me,
On the Cross of suffering bought me;
Shall such grace be vainly brought me?

Righteous Judge! for sin’s pollution
Grant Thy gift of absolution,
Ere that day of retribution.
Guilty, now I pour my moaning,
All my shame with anguish owning;
Spare, O God, Thy suppliant groaning.

Thou the sinful woman savedst;
Thou the dying thief forgavest;
And to me a hope vouchsafest.
Worthless are my prayers and sighing;
Yet, good Lord, in grace complying,
Rescue me from fires undying.

With Thy favour’d sheep O place me,
Nor among the goats abase me,
But to Thy right hand upraise me.
While the wicked are confounded,
Doom’d to flames of woe unbounded,
Call me with Thy Saints surrounded.

Low I kneel, with heart submission,
See, like ashes, my contrition;
Help me in my last condition.

Ah! that day of tears and mourning!
From the dust of earth returning
Man for judgment must prepare him:
Spare, O God, in mercy spare him!
Lord, all-pitying, Jesu Blest,
Grant them Thine eternal rest.
Amen.

translations.text: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, that our humble prayers in behalf of the souls of thy servants, both men and women, may be profitable to them: so that thou mayest deliver them from all their sins, and make them partakers of the redemption thou hast purchased for them. Who livest.

differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

Read at printed pp. 241-244 = leaves n278-n281, under `Sequence, Mass for the Dead.` and the incipit `Dies irae dies illa.` Nineteen stanzas against the Missal's nineteen strophes, one for one; the closing `Amen.` is not rendered. This corrected the recovered lane brief and the then-current guidance row, which had misidentified the London edition's contents. The London 1849 prints it, in its Missal section, between the Lauda Sion and the cross-reference to the Stabat Mater. An independent English of this sequence is therefore not needed for coverage; the alternative Irons text below is offered as a choice of voice, not as a gap-filler. translations.text:
Nigher still, and still more nigh
Draws the Day of Prophecy,
Doom’d to melt the earth and sky.

Oh, what trembling there shall be,
When the world its Judge shall see,
Coming in dread majesty!

Hark! the trump, with thrilling tone,
From sepulchral regions lone,
Summons all before the throne:

Time and Death it doth appal,
To see the buried ages all
Rise to answer at the call.

Now the books are open spread;
Now the writing must be read,
Which condemns the quick and dead:

Now, before the Judge severe
Hidden things must all appear;
Nought can pass unpunish’d here.

What shall guilty I then plead?
Who for me will intercede,
When the Saints shall comfort need?

King of dreadful Majesty!
Who dost freely justify!
Fount of Pity, save Thou me!

Recollect, O Love divine!
’Twas for this lost sheep of thine
Thou thy glory didst resign:

Satest wearied seeking me;
Sufferedst upon the Tree:
Let not vain thy labour be.

Judge of Justice, hear my prayer!
Spare me, Lord, in mercy spare!
Ere the Reckoning-day appear.

Lo! thy gracious face I seek;
Shame and grief are on my cheek;
Sighs and tears my sorrow speak.

Thou didst Mary’s guilt forgive;
Didst the dying thief receive;
Hence doth hope within me live.

Worthless are my prayers, I know;
Yet, oh, cause me not to go
Into everlasting woe.

Sever’d from the guilty band,
Make me with thy sheep to stand,
Placing me on thy right hand.

When the curs’d in anguish flee
Into flames of misery;
With the Blest then call Thou me.

Suppliant in the dust I lie;
My heart a cinder, crush’d and dry;
Help me, Lord, when death is nigh!

Full of tears, and full of dread,
Is the day that wakes the dead,
Calling all, with solemn blast,
From the ashes of the past.

Lord of mercy! Jesu blest!
Grant the Faithful light and rest.

translations.text:
Day of Wrath! O day of mourning!
See fulfill’d the prophets’ warning!
Heav’n and earth in ashes burning!
Oh, what fear man’s bosom rendeth
When from Heav’n the Judge descendeth,
On Whose sentence all dependeth!

Wondrous sound the trumpet flingeth,
Through earth’s sepulchres it ringeth,
All before the Throne it bringeth.
Death is struck, and nature quaking,
All creation is awaking,
To its Judge an answer making.

Lo! the Book exactly worded,
Wherein all hath been recorded;
Thence shall judgment be awarded.
When the Judge His seat attaineth,
And each hidden deed arraigneth,
Nothing unavenged remaineth.

What shall I, frail man, be pleading,
Who for me be interceding,
When the just are mercy needing?
King of Majesty tremendous,
Who dost free salvation send us,
Fount of pity, then befriend us!

Think, good Jesu, my salvation
Caused Thy wondrous Incarnation;
Leave me not to reprobation.
Faint and weary Thou hast sought me,
On the Cross of suffering bought me;
Shall such grace be vainly brought me?

Righteous Judge! for sin’s pollution
Grant Thy gift of absolution,
Ere that day of retribution.
Guilty, now I pour my moaning,
All my shame with anguish owning;
Spare, O God, Thy suppliant groaning.

Thou the sinful woman savedst;
Thou the dying thief forgavest;
And to me a hope vouchsafest.
Worthless are my prayers and sighing;
Yet, good Lord, in grace complying,
Rescue me from fires undying.

With Thy favour’d sheep O place me,
Nor among the goats abase me,
But to Thy right hand upraise me.
While the wicked are confounded,
Doom’d to flames of woe unbounded,
Call me with Thy Saints surrounded.

Low I kneel, with heart submission,
See, like ashes, my contrition;
Help me in my last condition.

Ah! that day of tears and mourning!
From the dust of earth returning
Man for judgment must prepare him:
Spare, O God, in mercy spare him!
Lord, all-pitying, Jesu Blest,
Grant them Thine eternal rest.
Amen.

translations.text:
Nigher still, and still more nigh
Draws the Day of Prophecy,
Doom’d to melt the earth and sky.

Oh, what trembling there shall be,
When the world its Judge shall see,
Coming in dread majesty!

Hark! the trump, with thrilling tone,
From sepulchral regions lone,
Summons all before the throne:

Time and Death it doth appal,
To see the buried ages all
Rise to answer at the call.

Now the books are open spread;
Now the writing must be read,
Which condemns the quick and dead:

Now, before the Judge severe
Hidden things must all appear;
Nought can pass unpunish’d here.

What shall guilty I then plead?
Who for me will intercede,
When the Saints shall comfort need?

King of dreadful Majesty!
Who dost freely justify!
Fount of Pity, save Thou me!

Recollect, O Love divine!
’Twas for this lost sheep of thine
Thou thy glory didst resign:

Satest wearied seeking me;
Sufferedst upon the Tree:
Let not vain thy labour be.

Judge of Justice, hear my prayer!
Spare me, Lord, in mercy spare!
Ere the Reckoning-day appear.

Lo! thy gracious face I seek;
Shame and grief are on my cheek;
Sighs and tears my sorrow speak.

Thou didst Mary’s guilt forgive;
Didst the dying thief receive;
Hence doth hope within me live.

Worthless are my prayers, I know;
Yet, oh, cause me not to go
Into everlasting woe.

Sever’d from the guilty band,
Make me with thy sheep to stand,
Placing me on thy right hand.

When the curs’d in anguish flee
Into flames of misery;
With the Blest then call Thou me.

Suppliant in the dust I lie;
My heart a cinder, crush’d and dry;
Help me, Lord, when death is nigh!

Full of tears, and full of dread,
Is the day that wakes the dead,
Calling all, with solemn blast,
From the ashes of the past.

Lord of mercy! Jesu blest!
Grant the Faithful light and rest.

translations.text:
Day of Wrath! O day of mourning!
See fulfill’d the prophets’ warning!
Heav’n and earth in ashes burning!
Oh, what fear man’s bosom rendeth
When from Heav’n the Judge descendeth,
On Whose sentence all dependeth!

Wondrous sound the trumpet flingeth,
Through earth’s sepulchres it ringeth,
All before the Throne it bringeth.
Death is struck, and nature quaking,
All creation is awaking,
To its Judge an answer making.

Lo! the Book exactly worded,
Wherein all hath been recorded;
Thence shall judgment be awarded.
When the Judge His seat attaineth,
And each hidden deed arraigneth,
Nothing unavenged remaineth.

What shall I, frail man, be pleading,
Who for me be interceding,
When the just are mercy needing?
King of Majesty tremendous,
Who dost free salvation send us,
Fount of pity, then befriend us!

Think, good Jesu, my salvation
Caused Thy wondrous Incarnation;
Leave me not to reprobation.
Faint and weary Thou hast sought me,
On the Cross of suffering bought me;
Shall such grace be vainly brought me?

Righteous Judge! for sin’s pollution
Grant Thy gift of absolution,
Ere that day of retribution.
Guilty, now I pour my moaning,
All my shame with anguish owning;
Spare, O God, Thy suppliant groaning.

Thou the sinful woman savedst;
Thou the dying thief forgavest;
And to me a hope vouchsafest.
Worthless are my prayers and sighing;
Yet, good Lord, in grace complying,
Rescue me from fires undying.

With Thy favour’d sheep O place me,
Nor among the goats abase me,
But to Thy right hand upraise me.
While the wicked are confounded,
Doom’d to flames of woe unbounded,
Call me with Thy Saints surrounded.

Low I kneel, with heart submission,
See, like ashes, my contrition;
Help me in my last condition.

Ah! that day of tears and mourning!
From the dust of earth returning
Man for judgment must prepare him:
Spare, O God, in mercy spare him!
Lord, all-pitying, Jesu Blest,
Grant them Thine eternal rest.
Amen.

Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n1316, ordinary printed p. 1302, under the Common of One or More Supreme Pontiffs and `Prayer`. The facing Latin is the 1962 singular Collect with its martyr alternative intact. This is ordinary numbered matter immediately before, and not part of, excluded pp. 1302a-1302d; no other Supreme-Pontiff row is recovered.

witnesses.label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1861 keeps this feast on the Second Sunday after Epiphany, not on the Sunday between 2 and 5 January as the 1962 does. Leaf n104, printed p. 94, heads it `II. SUNDAY after EPIPHANY. The FEAST of the HOLY NAME JESUS.` over the Introit `In nomine Jesu`, and its Kalendar at leaf n774, printed p. 766, prints `Second Sunday after Epiphany- Feast of the most Holy Name of Jesus, d. of II. class 94`. The formulary is the same one, and the Latin cue set before this English is `Deus qui`, which answers the 1962's `Deus, qui Unigenitum`. The day placement is a recension difference and not a difference of text. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: O God, who didst appoint thy only begotten Son the Saviour of mankind, and commandest that his name should be called JESUS: mercifully grant, that we who venerate his holy name on earth, may also enjoy his sight in heaven. Thro'.

translations.text: May thy blessing, O most merciful God, by which every creature is enlivened and subsists, sanctify this our sacrifice, which we offer thee in honour of the name of thy Son, our Lord Jesus Christ: that it may be acceptable to the praise of thy majesty, and available to our salvation. Thro' the same.

translations.text: O almighty and eternal God, who didst both create and redeem us, mercifully hear our prayers, and vouchsafe, with a pleasing and kind countenance, to receive the sacrifice of this victim of our salvation, which we have offered to thy divine majesty, in honor of the name of thy Son, our Lord Jesus Christ; that thy grace being poured on us, thro' the glorious name of Jesus, as a pledge of our eternal predestination, we may rejoice that our names are written in heaven. Thro' the same.

ordinary_frame.basis: This row withholds the whole bundled Palm Sunday entry because its blessing and procession are known to be the reformed service, while the boundary around the following Mass has not been collated or represented. Applying the ordinary frame to this unavailable bundle would present the 1861 Ordinary as though the withheld pre-1955 bundle had been established. The structural difference and its pre-1955 loci are recorded at roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml under `palmis.benedictio.*` and `palmis.distributio.*`.

also.basis: The 1962 book heads the day Dominica II Passionis seu in Palmis, and that title is the reform's own: Maxima Redemptionis fixes it in the sentence that says when the new Order begins, `Novus hic Ordo servari debet a die 25 Martii, dominica II Passionis seu in palmis, anni 1956` [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, departure maxima-redemptionis-1955/renamed, act cited at aas-47-1955 51853-51854]. The pre-1955 witnesses head it Dominica in Palmis [same file, mass dominica-in-palmis, attested by pustet-1862 28094 and missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body 31875-31877].

The Gospel of the entry into Jerusalem, Matthew 21, 1-9, is the same text in a different place in the service. The pre-1955 books read it BEFORE the blessing prayers [missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body 32017-32022, pustet-1862 28242-28247]; the 1962 book reads it AFTER the distribution of palms, under its own heading [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, unit palmis.benedictio.evangelium]. Neither book is missing it, which is why this is `reslotted` and not `absent` — the case the vocabulary was extended to name.

recension.basis: The inherited entry includes the reformed blessing and procession of palms. The pre-1955 books instead print the fourteen-unit service recorded under `palmis.benedictio.*` and `palmis.distributio.*`, while eleven of those units are absent from the 1962 witness [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml]. The Mass formulary after the procession has not been collated separately. Because the base bundles the known- different service with that Mass, serving the base entry would present reformed Holy Week material under a pre-1955 heading; this row therefore withholds the whole bundled entry until the boundary can be represented.

recension.basis: Maxima Redemptionis moved the Mass of the Lord's Supper to the evening; section 7 of the decree carries the provision [aas-47-1955 51905-51908, recorded at roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, departure maxima-redemptionis-1955/moved, mass feria-v-in-coena-domini]. The hour the pre-1955 books appoint is NOT ESTABLISHED: the act history's own mass row records `hour = "not established"` for this liturgy, where it fixes an hour for the other three. It is recorded moved because the decree says it moved, and the origin is left unstated rather than inferred from the general rubric on the hours of Mass.

ordinary_frame.basis: Feria VI in Parasceve is the exceptional Good Friday service, not a Mass formulary to be seated in the Ordinary transcribed from the 1861 lay missal. Its pre-1955 identity and hour were read at missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body 35401-35408 and pustet-1862 31916, and its known unit-level differences are recorded at roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml under `parasceve.*`.

also.basis: The pre-1955 books celebrate the liturgy of Good Friday in the morning, in choir after None [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, mass feria-vi-in-parasceve, attested by pustet-1862 31916 and missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body 35401-35403 with the hour at 35408]. Maxima Redemptionis moved it to the afternoon in terms: `Feria VI in Passione et Morte Domini solemnis actio liturgica celebratur horis postmeridianis` [aas-47-1955 51910-51911].

The same sentence renames the day. The pre-1955 heading is Feria VI in Parasceve; the reformed books head it Feria VI in Passione et Morte Domini and print that title in their running heads [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, departure maxima-redemptionis-1955/renamed].

The solemn prayer for the Jews differs between the witnesses in its invitatory, its rubric and its oration, and NO ACT FOR THE CHANGE WAS FOUND. The act history records all three as `unrecorded` and refuses to attach them to the 1962 edition merely because that is the first witness in which the words are gone [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, departures editio-typica-1962/unrecorded, units parasceve.orationes.pro-iudaeis-*]. It is carried here rather than dropped so that a page serving pre-1955 Good Friday cannot claim the base's text was checked for these units.

recension.basis: The solemn prayer for the Jews differs in its invitatory, rubric and oration between the pre-1955 witnesses and the inherited 1962 entry [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, units parasceve.orationes.pro-iudaeis-*]. The correspondence of the complete service has not been established. Serving the inherited formulary would therefore present known-different words under the pre-1955 heading, so this row serves no formulary wording.

ordinary_frame.basis: The pre-1955 Holy Saturday bundle has twelve prophecies, a Mass with no Postcommunion, and Vespers where the reformed entry has another structure. None of that pre-1955 wording is transcribed here, and the service has not been separated into a frame that can safely borrow the 1861 Ordinary. The established structure and witness loci are recorded at roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml under `sabbato.prophetiae.01` through `.12`, `sabbato.missa.*`, and `sabbato.vesperae.*`.

also.basis: The largest single departure in this file. The pre-1955 service is held on Saturday MORNING: it begins `Dicta Nona in Choro`, and the general rubric De hora celebrandi Missam allows Mass only `ab aurora usque ad meridiem` [missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body 37276 and 9614-9615, pustet-1862 33479 and 8151-8152; recorded at roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, mass sabbato-sancto, with the reasoning for the hour set out in `hour_basis` because no rubric in either witness fixes an hour in words]. Section 9 of Maxima Redemptionis moved it to the night, and the act history calls the evidence for this its strongest single piece: the decree's sentence at aas-47-1955 51915-51921 is reproduced WORD FOR WORD in the 1962 witness at benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 40203-40212.

The day keeps its name and the liturgy within it is renamed: the decree speaks of the `solemnis paschalis vigilia` [aas-47-1955 51915] and the reformed book prints SABBATO SANCTO with DE VIGILIA PASCHALI beneath it [benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962 40187, 40195].

The case this repository's recension model was built to carry, and the one that generated false absences before it existed. The pre-1955 Mass of Holy Saturday HAS NO POSTCOMMUNION — its own rubric suppresses one — and the office that follows is VESPERS, whose Oratio is the prayer Spiritum nobis. The reformed book suppresses no Postcommunion and prints one, and the office that follows is LAUDS of the Resurrection, with Benedictus for Magnificat and the antiphon Valde mane for Vespere autem sabbati [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, units sabbato.missa.rubrica-nec-postcommunio and sabbato.vesperae.*]. A matcher keyed on (mass, proper-name) asked the pre-1955 book for a slot the reform created, got nothing, and wrote down an absence; the words were on the page the whole time, in another slot.

recension.basis: The pre-1955 books print twelve prophecies where the reformed book prints four lessons, suppress a Postcommunion, and follow the Mass with Vespers rather than Lauds [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, units sabbato.prophetiae.01 through .12, sabbato.missa.* and sabbato.vesperae.*]. Those are known structural and textual differences, while no pre-1955 wording has been verified for service here. The inherited reformed Vigil is therefore replaced by a typed unavailable formulary state.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

Read at Internet Archive item LyraCatholica1849, printed pp. 233-234 = leaves n270-n271, under the heading `Sequence, Easter-Sunday.` and the Latin incipit `Victimae Paschali laudes.` Six English stanzas answer the Missal's eight strophes, the fifth stanza carrying `Sepulcrum Christi viventis` and `Angelicos testes` together. The Missal's closing `Amen. Alleluja.` is not rendered; Caswall prints no acclamation.

translations.text:
Forth to the paschal Victim, Christians, bring
Your sacrifice of praise:

The Lamb redeems the sheep;
And Christ, the Sinless One,
Hath to the Father sinners reconcil’d.

Together, Death and Life
In a strange conflict strove;
The Prince of Life, who died,
Now lives and reigns.

What thou sawest, Mary, say,
As thou wentest on the way.

I saw the tomb wherein the Living One had lain;
I saw his glory as He rose again;
Napkin and linen clothes, and Angels twain:
Yea, Christ is risen, my hope, and He
Will go before you into Galilee.

We know that Christ indeed has risen from the grave:
Hail, thou King of Victory!
Have mercy, Lord, and save.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 598 in the Mass of Whitsunday, facing Latin and English. The English renders every word of the 1962 body, with the same alleluias; a printed scripture citation is omitted as in the Latin body, any cue stands as the book prints it, and nothing is supplied from the excluded inserts. Read at 200 dpi and at the scan's native 300 dpi. Cummiskey 1861 at printed p. 375 (IA leaf n383) is not bound: both its English and its own Latin cue end the antiphon with two alleluias where the 1962 prints three, so it witnesses a different text.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: The Spirit of the Lord hath filled the whole earth, alleluia; and that which containeth all things hath knowledge of the voice, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Ps. Let God arise, and His enemies be scattered; and let them that hate Him fly before His face. V. Glory.

witnesses.label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 375 in the formulary the book heads WHIT SUNDAY; the printed Latin cue answers the 1962 Collect, and the English renders it clause for clause. The dated page-image verification passage and the separate tracked public-domain passage bind this body; the wording also agrees with row 104 of temporal-orations-en. The Cummiskey witness remains a pre-1955 lay hand missal; this row makes no broader recension claim. Second reading: the Lasance New Roman Missal (1945 revision, printed about 1955-56) at printed p. 598, IA leaf n595, passage passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.whitsunday-collect, read on 2026-10-19, is an independent translation that also renders every clause of the 1962 Latin. It is recorded here and not served beside this body, because an entry bound to a publication passage carries exactly one witness's translation.

translations.text: Continuation of the holy Gospel according to St. John. At that time, Jesus said to His disciples, If any one love Me, he will keep My word, and My Father will love him, and we will come to him, and will make our abode with him. He that loveth Me not, keepeth not My words: and the word which you have heard is not Mine, but the Father's Who sent Me. These things have I spoken to you, abiding with you: but the Paraclete, the Holy Ghost, Whom the Father will send in My name, He will teach you all things, and bring all things to your mind, whatsoever I shall have said to you. Peace I leave with you, My peace I give unto you; not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid. You have heard that I said to you, I go away, and I come unto you. If you loved Me, you would indeed be glad, because I go to the Father, for the Father is greater than I. And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it shall come to pass, you may believe. I will not now speak many things with you; for the prince of this world cometh, and in Me he hath not anything. But that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father hath given Me commandments, so do I.

stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

ordinary_frame.basis: The source prints both a longer and a shorter form. Each appoints a Lesson and Alleluia before a later Epistle and Sequence; the longer form appoints five Lessons and its intervening chants. The generic Ordinary frame has no form-sensitive repeated-reading module, and the Order-of-Mass inventory explicitly leaves the later Ember chants unplaced. A specialized frame has not yet been modeled, so every row remains source-ordered while the generic frame is withheld.

Read at printed pp. 236-240 = leaves n273-n277, under `Sequence, Solemnity of Corpus Christi.` and the incipit `Lauda Sion Salvatorem.` Twelve stanzas against the Missal's twenty-four strophes, two for one throughout. The printing sets the bracketed marker `[Ecce panis angelorum.]` at the head of the eleventh stanza, which is the strophe at which the postconciliar shorter form begins. The Missal's closing `Amen. translations.text:
Sion, lift thy voice, and sing;
Praise thy Saviour and thy King;
Praise with hymns thy Shepherd true:
Strive thy best to praise Him well;
Yet doth He all praise excel;
None can ever reach His due.

See to-day before us laid
The living and life-giving Bread!
Theme for praise and joy profound!
The same which at the sacred board
Was, by our Incarnate Lord,
Giv’n to his Apostles round.

Let the praise be loud and high;
Sweet and tranquil be the joy
Felt to-day in every breast;
On this Festival divine,
Which records the origin
Of the glorious Eucharist.

On this Table of the King,
Our new Paschal offering
Brings to end the olden rite;
Here, for empty shadows fled,
Is Reality instead;
Here, instead of darkness, Light.

His own act, at supper seated,
Christ ordain’d to be repeated,
In His Memory divine;
Wherefore now, with adoration,
We the Host of our salvation
Consecrate from bread and wine.

Hear what holy Church maintaineth,
That the bread its substance changeth
Into Flesh, the wine to Blood.
Doth it pass thy comprehending?
Faith, the law of sight transcending,
Leaps to things not understood.

Here, beneath these signs, are hidden
Priceless things, to sense forbidden;
Signs, not things, are all we see;—
Flesh from bread, and Blood from wine;
Yet is Christ, in either sign,
All entire, confess’d to be.

They too, who of Him partake,
Sever not, nor rend, nor break,
But entire, their Lord receive.
Whether one or thousands eat,
All receive the self-same meat,
Nor the less for others leave.

Both the wicked and the good
Eat of this celestial Food;
But with ends how opposite!
Here ’tis life; and there ’tis death;
The same, yet issuing to each
In a difference infinite.

Nor a single doubt retain,
When they break the Host in twain,
But that in each part remains
What was in the whole before;
Since the simple sign alone
Suffers change in state or form,
The Signified remaining One
And the Same for evermore.

Lo! upon the Altar lies,
Hidden deep from human eyes,
Bread of Angels from the skies,
Made the food of mortal man:
Children’s meat to dogs denied;
In old types foresignified;
In the manna Heav’n-supplied,
Isaac, and the Paschal Lamb.

Jesu! Shepherd of the sheep!
Thou thy flock in safety keep.
Living Bread! thy life supply;
Strengthen us, or else we die;
Fill us with celestial grace:
Thou, who feedest us below!
Source of all we have or know!
Grant that with thy Saints above,
Sitting at the feast of love,
We may see Thee face to face.

ordinary_frame.basis: This is the blessing and distribution of palms which precedes the Mass, not a Mass formulary to be seated in the Ordo Missae. Its fourteen units, including its own Preface and Sanctus, are recorded from the 1862 witness and the later composite's 1951-1954 body at roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml under `palmis.benedictio.*` and `palmis.distributio.*`.

recension.basis: The pre-1955 blessing of palms is a service of fourteen units the 1962 book does not print, and it is `added` rather than a difference within Palm Sunday because the base holds no entry for it at all. Eleven of the fourteen are recorded `absent` at the 1955 station with a per-unit basis [roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml, units palmis.benedictio.* and palmis.distributio.*, each attested by pustet-1862 and missale-romanum-later-composite-pre-1955-body with loci]. Among them are a Lectio from Exodus, a Graduale, a full Preface and Sanctus, and six orations; the 1962 blessing runs from the antiphon straight to a single blessing prayer.

blockers.requirement: Page-collate inherited wording and its calendar joins against the accepted Bonn 2004 reimpressio of the conformed 28th edition of about 1954, with the 1922 Mame conformed printing as the control for later additions. The completed section-body inventory establishes identities, not wording agreement or per-Proper attestation. An exact Vatican 1920 impression remains unauthenticated; acquiring it is not a prerequisite under the maintainer's 2026-10-19 witness decision. OCR may locate text but may not supply it.
Give every Proper a per-witness attestation before residence is moved from roman-1962 or inherited text is described as pre-1955.
Read a pre-1955 general calendar from page images, including grades, octaves, and vigils; do not reconstruct it by subtracting 1962.

Model the five ordered criteria directly, including the different role of propriety in occurrence and concurrence, and replace the present numbered linearization with source-shaped evaluation and solved cases.
Locate the 1900 typical edition that the 1920 decree names as its parent, closing the act history's one `via_unrepresented` edge.
Read the restricted 1956 Ordo in a lawful accessible copy and model the 1956-1960 middle state before attributing every pre-1955-to-1962 Holy Week difference to the 1955 reform.
Keep the blessing of oils outside the Missal claim until an identified pre-1955 Pontificale Romanum edition is registered and read.

calendar.basis: Six Holy Week departures and two exact post-1954 sanctoral absences are stated. The remainder of the temporal and sanctoral calendar is inherited from roman-1962 without a pre-1955 kalendarium collation, including the octaves and vigils affected by the March 1955 simplification.

ceremonies.basis: The act history records structural units for Palm Sunday and the Triduum from OCR and promulgating acts. It expressly excludes a complete ceremonial, notation, the Office, and unstated units.

commons.basis: Every Common is inherited from roman-1962. No pre-1955 witness has been collated against those formularies, so inheritance proves availability in the projection and not identity in the target recension.

ordinary.basis: A separate Ordinary inventory transcribes the 1861 Cummiskey lay missal, including its facing Latin where printed. It is neither the 1920 altar book nor an element-by-element collation against that typical edition.

precedence.basis: The companion rubrics source openly linearizes the five Divino afflatu criteria into numbered rows. It records divergences and supports a finding aid, but it does not implement the criteria as criteria.

propers.basis: No Proper wording in this departure file is transcribed from or page-collated against the 1920 typical edition. Known-different bundled formularies carry typed unavailable status and no pseudo-Proper rows; unstated formularies are mechanical roman-1962 fallback, not pre-1955 attestations.

evidence.basis: The inventory records the unit-level structure and acts behind these Holy Week departures, while refusing its OCR readings as witnesses to wording. Its source formerly labelled as the 1920 printing is a later composite, body 1951-1954 with a post-1970 appendix; that OCR is held only as a structural/search witness and does not establish exact target-edition correspondence.
Titulus II of the 1911 rubrics was read in the publisher PDF. The current table is a disclosed linearization of its five criteria rather than a claim that the source printed numbered precedence rows.
The 1861 witness was transcribed from page images at the grades its inventory states. This establishes that witness only, not the wording of the 1920 typical edition.

`[the_1920_substitution.where_it_cannot]`, item 3, and `[the_1920_substitution.a_defect_in_the_1920_artifact_itself].finding` record the separately verified absence of the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary and St Joseph the Worker from the pre-reform witness body. The artifact record bounds that body to 1951-1954, records zero `Opific` hits, and records `Reginae` only in old local-indult material. The same inventory item's St Pius X negative was corrected as false, so these rows rely only on the two retained and reverified results and make no claim about St Pius X.

inheritance.basis: `text_from` is a mechanical fallback to the only target altar-book corpus transcribed in this repository. It does not assert that any unstated 1962 entry was checked in a pre-1955 witness or remained unchanged.

translations.caution: A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
translations.label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)

translations.caution: A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.
translations.label: Lyra Catholica: containing all the Breviary and Missal hymns, with others from various sources, translated by Edward Caswall (London: James Burns, 1849)

translations.caution:
THIS IS HYMNS ANCIENT AND MODERN'S TEXT OF IRONS AND NOT DEMONSTRABLY IRONS'S
OWN. That book's compilers are widely said to have altered what they received;
this lane established no instance of alteration in this hymn and ran no collation
against a printing of Irons's own, because none was located. The claim that this
is Irons's translation rests on the 1889 Historical Companion's attribution, read
on its page image; the claim that it is UNALTERED rests on nothing and is not
made.

Most of the hymn is set under vocal score in this printing, so 22 of its 58 lines
were read syllable by syllable from under the staves. That is the weakest point
of the transcription.
translations.label: Hymns Ancient and Modern, Complete Edition with accompanying tunes (London: printed for the proprietors by William Clowes and Sons), hymn 398, W. J. Irons's English of the Dies irae
